mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy cycle, compressing discount rates applied to equity cash flows, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) despite a sustained decline in FEDFUNDS for at least 3 months, or FEDFUNDS shows no sustained decline over the period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward movement in the unemployment rate above 6.5% triggers a loss of investor confidence in labor market recovery, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3 percentage points in 3 months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) despite UNRATE crossing the 6.5% threshold, or the rate does not cross the threshold within the period.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent rises in both demand (GDPC1) and supply (INDPRO) indices signal a robust economic expansion, boosting corporate earnings and equity valuations, which drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) despite both GDPC1 and INDPRO rising concurrently, or their combined effect does not correlate with positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: In a recession recovery regime, a sustained rise in demand (GDPC1) above 2% in 3 months predicts stronger economic growth and improved corporate performance, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 rises > 2 percentage points in 3 months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) despite GDPC1 meeting the threshold, or the regime is not in recession recovery when the trigger occurs.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in both demand (HOUST) and labor participation (PAYEMS) indices indicate robust economic activity, which expands corporate profits and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) despite both HOUST and PAYEMS rising concurrently, or their combined effect does not correlate with positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in supply growth (INDPRO falling below 101.5 in 3 months) signals contractionary pressures, reducing corporate earnings growth and equity valuations, which drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 1 percentage point in 3 months
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) despite INDPRO falling below the threshold, or the rate does not fall sufficiently within the period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5.5% signals improving labor market conditions, boosting consumer confidence and corporate investment, which drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) despite UNRATE declining for at least 3 months, or UNRATE does not decline sufficiently.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals investor expectations of higher inflation, leading to reduced equity valuations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5 percentage points in 3 months
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) despite FEDFUNDS rising above the threshold within the tightening cycle, or the regime is not in tightening when the trigger occurs.
